slideDifferences.nativeText:
PHRASES
MEANING
EXAMPLE
A SMOKING GUN
Something that is obvious; an indisputable truth.
You should have seen the smoking gun; that man could not be trusted.
HIDDEN AGENDA
Something that may refer to a secret plan or an implication.
I would not have expected Freddy to have a hidden agenda.
A SHOT IN THE DARK
To have an ide or suspicion about someone or something.
Thank God I had already gotten a shot in the dark about Tim, he almost got away with that.
NUTS AND BOLTS
The detailed information about someone or something and how it works.
If it had been me, I would have gone nut and bolts with Jenny; now she’s gone!
AN INSIDE STORY
Considered as an advice or a hot tip.
What an inside story John has just dropped us.
A STRAW IN THE WIND
It refers to an indication or sign that one can see or get from someone or something.
We should have seen the straw in the wind; now, we can’t do anything.
UPPER HAND
It means someone or something has a position of advantage and control.
Fortunately, I had already upper-handed the rest of the contestants.
TIP OF THE ICEBERG
The small piece or amount of something that we can see.
Handing over the project was just the tip of the iceberg.
Look at the phrases and  discuss them with your teacher. Did you know them?

slideDifferences.nativeText:
We are able to express opinions, suggestions and expectations in the past by using the following structures. Check the chart.
STRUCTURES
STATEMENTS
QUESTIONS
Should  Have + Past Participle
Dylan should have called them before going.
What should he have done before going?
If it had been me, I should have brought more money.
What should you have done?
Would  have + Past Participle
My family would have wanted him to be different, but he wasn’t.
How would have your family wanted him to be?
He would not have expected me to drop school.
would he have expected you to drop school?
Must have + Past Participle
We must have seen the straw in the wind, but we did not.
Would you have seen the straw in the wind?
If he had done things differently, the boss would have given him the chance.
What if he had done things differently?

He would not have expected me to drop school. Would he have expected you to drop school? Must have + Past Participle We must have seen the straw in the wind, but we did not. slideDifferences.nativeText:
To Consider

This structures do not necessarily work using the third conditional. 
Modals + Have + past participle are still the base of the structure.
We can use yes/no questions or Wh-words to go interrogative. 
The context or the joining statements attached to these grammar structures are important and they need to be cohesive and logical. 
All of them state a hypothetical or unreal situation in the past.

C. Read the following paragraph and have a discussion with the teacher. After that, read aloud the text to your teacher.
'Friends' cast sings show's theme song with James Corden

James Corden, host of the reunion that we all couldn't stop talking about, recruited the cast of "Friends" for a special segment that aired on his show Wednesday night.
In the clip, Corden helps transport the cast -- Jennifer Aniston, Courteney Cox, Lisa Kudrow, Matt LeBlanc, Matthew Perry and David Schwimmer -- to the set and uses the brief ride through the Warner Bros. lot, where they used to film, to channel "Carpool Karaoke." Do you really need to ask the song choice? We all would have chosen the same, wouldn’t we?


After belting The Rembrandt's "I'll Be There For You," Corden and the cast get cozy in Central Perk for some fun and games, that turns some on the couches to tears as we all must’ve expected. "Friends: The Reunion" was released last month on HBO Max. (CNN, like HBO, is owned by WarnerMedia.) and it was said to be the last episode (reunion) of the cast despite fans would have desired it to be one of many to come. 

While the streamer has not released viewing numbers, Variety reported that the highly-anticipated special may have performed nearly as well as "Wonder Woman 1984," the sequel to the 2017 blockbuster superhero film. Nevertheless, it is a fact that thousands if not millions of people watched the reunion and we would not have expected less from a TV show that is clearly part of pop culture and an iconic program for masses. 

Article adapted from https://edition.cnn.com/2021/06/17/entertainment/friends-james-corden/index.html

texts: PHRASES
MEANING
EXAMPLE
A SMOKING GUN
Something that is obvious; an indisputable truth.
You should have seen the smoking gun; that man could not be trusted.
HIDDEN AGENDA
Something that may refer to a secret plan or an implication.
I would not have expected Freddy to have a hidden agenda.
A SHOT IN THE DARK
To have an ide or suspicion about someone or something.
Thank God I had already gotten a shot in the dark about Tim, he almost got away with that.
NUTS AND BOLTS
The detailed information about someone or something and how it works.
If it had been me, I would have gone nut and bolts with Jenny; now she’s gone!
AN INSIDE STORY
Considered as an advice or a hot tip.
What an inside story John has just dropped us.
A STRAW IN THE WIND
It refers to an indication or sign that one can see or get from someone or something.
We should have seen the straw in the wind; now, we can’t do anything.
UPPER HAND
It means someone or something has a position of advantage and control.
Fortunately, I had already upper-handed the rest of the contestants.
TIP OF THE ICEBERG
The small piece or amount of something that we can see.
Handing over the project was just the tip of the iceberg.
Look at the phrases and  discuss them with your teacher. Did you know them?

We can use yes/no questions or Wh-words to go interrogative. 
The context or the joining statements attached to these grammar structures are important and they need to be cohesive and logical. 
All of them state a hypothetical or unreal situation in the past.

Functions
Examples
State suggestions about past events
Mary should have bought that car but she didn’t.
Express expectations about past events
We all  would have wanted Lyla to win the contest; maybe next year.
State an opinion in the past

We must have called the boss; now, we are in trouble. 

He must have left the house; It’s 11:00 PM already. *
To consider
*We can also use Must Have to state something truly happened out of deduction and regular behavior.

texts: C. Read the following paragraph and have a discussion with the teacher. After that, read aloud the text to your teacher.
'Friends' cast sings show's theme song with James Corden
James Corden, host of the reunion that we all couldn't stop talking about, recruited the cast of "Friends" for a special segment that aired on his show Wednesday night.

In the clip, Corden helps transport the cast -- Jennifer Aniston, Courteney Cox, Lisa Kudrow, Matt LeBlanc, Matthew Perry and David Schwimmer -- to the set and uses the brief ride through the Warner Bros. lot, where they used to film, to channel "Carpool Karaoke." Do you really need to ask the song choice? We all would have chosen the same, wouldn’t we?

After belting The Rembrandt's "I'll Be There For You," Corden and the cast get cozy in Central Perk for some fun and games, that turns some on the couches to tears as we all must’ve expected. "Friends: The Reunion" was released last month on HBO Max. (CNN, like HBO, is owned by WarnerMedia.) and it was said to be the last episode (reunion) of the cast despite fans would have desired it to be one of many to come.

While the streamer has not released viewing numbers, Variety reported that the highly-anticipated special may have performed nearly as well as "Wonder Woman 1984," the sequel to the 2017 blockbuster superhero film. Nevertheless, it is a fact that thousands if not millions of people watched the reunion and we would not have expected less from a TV show that is clearly part of pop culture and an iconic program for masses.
Article adapted from https://edition.cnn.com/2021/06/17/entertainment/friends-james-corden/index.html
